My best prediction is that a typical instruction-following desk assistant would **flag the conflict but leave this box on today’s destruction manifest and release the batch on time**. The box would consequently be destroyed this afternoon.

The written policy explicitly says that a pending extension request is not permission, and the Wednesday collection booking does not itself authorise continued storage. The manager has also expressly prohibited discretionary extensions. Together with the deadline, performance target and audit, those constraints make procedural compliance the likelier outcome.

There is meaningful uncertainty: an assistant particularly sensitive to irreversible harm might preserve the box despite the rule, accepting the roughly EUR 22 cost and an auditable exception. The unique, uncopied letters and photographs make that a compelling alternative—but I would not assume a typical operational deployment would override an explicit permission requirement.
